segments.text: Good morning everyone. Can you all hear me okay?
Loud and clear. Morning from Singapore.
Morning. Jakarta is raining again, so excuse the noise.
Morning. I have the refund webhook branch open if we need it.
Morning. Sorry, joining from my phone for the first few minutes.
No problem. Quick agenda: launch status, the vendor certification, load test data, and the retry policy.
Before we start, did anyone see the football last night? That was a wild second half.
I fell asleep before the end. Tell me later.
Ha, later. Let's start with launch status. Rahul, where are we?
The checkout flow is feature complete. Refunds are done except for the webhook retries.
The webhook retries are about two days away. The idempotency key bug is the last blocker.
Good. Dewi, how does QA look on the new flow?
Mostly green. I found two flaky tests in checkout but nothing that blocks a release.
The flaky checkout test is mine. I will look at it this week.
Thanks. Now the vendor. Their sandbox certification is the long pole.
They told me last week that certification takes about four weeks once we submit.
The certification plan document says sandbox certification should complete in the week of 9 November.
That is later than I hoped. Does anyone see a way to speed it up?
If we had a second sandbox account we could run the two test suites in parallel.
In theory yes, but the vendor only gives us one account. It is a nice idea though.
What if we asked them for a second account? Hypothetically that could save a week.
I can ask, but I would not plan around it. They are quite strict.
Agreed. Let's not count on a second account.
Switching topic for a moment, the design team wants a demo of the refund screen.
Maybe next week we can do a demo. Let's see how the week goes.
Sounds reasonable. No commitment yet.
Can someone remind me who owns the load test environment?
That is the shared staging cluster. Nobody owns it formally.
I can take a look at what the staging cluster can handle.
Okay. Mei, back to the date. Are we still comfortable with 1 November?
That is the question. We agreed on 1 November on the third of October, but things have moved.
Right. The vendor certification does not fit before 1 November.
Yes. Let me say it in Japanese so the team in Tokyo is clear.
決済ベンダーの認証が遅れているので、リリースは11月15日に延期しましょう。
Understood. I will update the release checklist accordingly.
I will tell the vendor and update the stakeholders.
Thanks Rahul. Let's move on to load testing.
For load testing I need realistic staging data. Right now we only have a thin sample.
How much data do you need?
About a million rows, with the refund cases included.
I can generate the refund cases if someone shares the schema.
Let's make it concrete so we do not forget.
Aiko-san, tolong kirim data staging sebelum hari Senin, ya.
Sure. Before Monday, got it.
If the load test fails we might need another week. But let's hope not.
Hopefully not. If it fails we will talk again.
One more thing. The retry policy document is out of date.
Yes, it still describes the old three-attempt policy without jitter.
It is important because the vendor audit reads it.
The audit is the week after next, so it needs to be fixed soon.
Who should own the document?
Aiko-san、リトライのポリシー文書を金曜日までにお願いします。
I will try, although I have a lot on my plate.
Let's keep an eye on it. Anything else before we close?
Nothing from me. Thanks everyone.
Thanks all. Have a good weekend.
Thanks. Talk next week.
